title: North Texas Invasive Species Barrier Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on April 28, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

North Texas Invasive Species Barrier Act of 2014 - Exempts certain water transfers by the North Texas Municipal Water District and the Greater Texoma Utility Authority from prohibitions on the transfer of invasive species across state borders proscribed under the Lacey Act Amendments of 1981 and related criminal code provisions if: (1) only closed systems from Lake Texoma are used in the transfer, and (2) invasive species are eliminated or removed at treatment facilities.

summary.headline: A 2014 federal law lets two North Texas water agencies move water from Lake Texoma across state lines despite certain invasive-species transfer bans, under specific conditions.
summary.what_it_does: The law creates an exception to federal rules that normally bar moving invasive species across state borders under the Lacey Act and related criminal provisions. The exception covers water transfers by the North Texas Municipal Water District and the Greater Texoma Utility Authority. To qualify, the transfers must use only closed systems that draw from Lake Texoma, and invasive species must be eliminated or removed at treatment facilities.

who_it_affects.how: It can carry out water transfers from Lake Texoma without being subject to the cross-state invasive species transfer bans, as long as it meets the closed-system and treatment conditions.
It can carry out water transfers from Lake Texoma without being subject to the cross-state invasive species transfer bans, as long as it meets the closed-system and treatment conditions.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive water from these two agencies' systems
who_it_affects.how: Their water supply may come through transfers that are allowed under this exception, which requires invasive species to be removed at treatment facilities.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date. The law was enacted on June 9, 2014.
